| GET | **`/foxxycode/mcp`** | Merged MCP server list from three levels: **`mcp_servers`** in **config.yaml** and the user-global **`<home>/mcp.json`** (both scope **`global`**), plus the project-local **`.foxxycode/mcp.json`** (scope **`local`**); mcp.json files are Cursor-compatible and later levels override earlier ones by name. JSON **`{"object":"foxxycode.mcp_list","items":[...]}`**; each item has **`name`**, **`source`** (**`global`** / **`local`**), **`origin`** (**`config`** / **`home`** / **`project`** — the owning file), **`readonly`** (**`true`** for config.yaml entries), **`transport`**, **`command`**, **`args`**, **`url`**, **`env`**, **`enabled`**, **`status`** (**`connected`** / **`error`** / **`disabled`** / **`unsupported`** / **`needs_approval`** / **`denied`**), **`error`**, **`source_path`** (file the declaration was read from), **`trusted`**, **`gated`**, **`fingerprint`** (digest an approval binds to), **`tools`** (**`[{name, description, enabled}]`**), **`disabled_tools`**. The response also carries **`workspace`** and **`project_trust`**. Enabled servers are probed for tools over their transport (**`stdio`** spawn, **`http`** streamable with legacy-SSE fallback, **`sse`**; connect, **`tools/list`**, close) with results cached until the definition changes; **`?refresh=1`** re-probes. Unknown transport types report **`unsupported`** without probing. A project-local entry arrives with the checkout, so it is **not** probed until it is approved for this workspace: such a row comes back with **`status: "needs_approval"`**, **`trusted: false`**, no tools, and the command an approval would cover. Under **`mcp.project_trust: deny`** the status is **`denied`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}/enable`** | Clears the server's disabled flag, persisting into the file that defines it (**config.yaml** **`disabled`** or **`disabled`** in the owning mcp.json), then reloads config. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** for an unknown server. Live sessions pick the change up on their next turn. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}/disable`** | Sets the server's disabled flag in the owning file. Same responses as **`enable`**. New sessions skip connecting the server; live sessions stop seeing its tools on the next turn. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}/tools/{tool}/enable`** | Removes **`{tool}`** from the server's disabled-tools list (**`disabled_tools`** in YAML, **`disabledTools`** in the owning mcp.json). **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** for an unknown server. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}/tools/{tool}/disable`** | Adds **`{tool}`** to the server's disabled-tools list. The tool is hidden from the agent's tool list and rejected at dispatch. Same responses as the tool **`enable`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}/trust`** | Approves the **current** declaration of a project-local (**`.foxxycode/mcp.json`**) server for this workspace, so sessions may start it. The approval is bound to the workspace and to a digest of the command-bearing declaration (transport, command, args, env, url, headers) and is stored in **`<home>/mcp-trust.json`** with a receipt naming what was approved (env and header **names** only, never values). Rewriting the entry withdraws it. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"fingerprint":"sha256:..."}`**; **`400`** for an unknown server, for one defined in **config.yaml** or **`<home>/mcp.json`** (they need no approval), and under **`mcp.project_trust: deny`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}/untrust`** | Withdraws the workspace approval. Sessions already holding a connected client keep it; new sessions no longer start the server. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"removed":bool}`** — **`removed`** reports whether an approval was on file. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/mcp/project-trust`** | Persists **`mcp.project_trust`** into config.yaml and reloads it. Body **`{"policy":"ask"\|"allow"\|"deny"}`**. **`ask`** (default) keeps project-local servers cold until each declaration is approved for its workspace; **`allow`** starts them automatically; **`deny`** never loads them. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"project_trust":"..."}`**; **`400`** for an unknown value. The bundled UI edits this in the MCP tab, next to the servers it governs, so it never joins the settings-document save flow. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/subagents`** | Subagent definitions visible from a workspace (**`?cwd=<absolute path>`**, default: the cwd a new session would get — the current project when one is set, else the server's default cwd, because that is the cwd **`spawn_agent`** decides trust against; a relative path is **`400`**): the embedded built-ins (**`general`**, **`explore`**), user-scope files under **`${FOXXYCODE_HOME}/agents`**, and project-scope files under the workspace's **`.claude/agents`** and **`.foxxycode/agents`** (**`subagents.dirs`**, later directories win by name). **`{"object":"foxxycode.subagent_list","workspace","policy","items":[...]}`** where **`workspace`** is the canonical path receipts are keyed by, **`policy`** the effective **`subagents.project_trust`**, and each item carries **`name`**, **`description`**, **`scope`** (**`builtin`**, **`user`**, **`project`**), **`path`**, **`digest`** (SHA-256 of the definition bytes, the embedded bytes for built-ins), **`model`**, **`mode`**, **`builtin`**, **`hidden`**, the bounds the definition declares — **`tools`**, **`disallowed_tools`**, **`permission_mode`**, **`timeout_seconds`**, **`max_turns`**, **`background`**, and **`role_bytes`** (the size of the role body; the body itself is never served, since a client would render it before anyone approved the file) — and the trust decision for that workspace: **`trust`** (**`trusted`** or **`needs_approval`**) mirrored as the booleans **`trusted`** and **`needs_approval`**. A field a definition does not declare is absent rather than empty: absent means "inherits". Under **`deny`** project directories are not read at all. See **`docs/features/subagents.md`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/subagents/{name}/trust`** | Approves the **current** content of a project-scope definition for a workspace: records a receipt in **`<home>/subagents-trust.json`** bound to the canonical workspace, the name and the file digest, so **`spawn_agent`** may run it under **`project_trust: ask`**. Rewriting the file withdraws the approval. Optional body **`{"cwd": ...}`** (default: the cwd a new session would get, as above); **`cwd`** must be the session's **server-side** workspace, the `cwd` field of the **`GET /foxxycode/sessions`** rows or **`GET /foxxycode/workspace/context`** with the session header, since receipts are keyed by that path. This route is the approval path for a remote console or ACP client, whose local `foxxycode agents trust` writes a receipt on the wrong machine. **`200`** **`{"object":"foxxycode.subagent","item":<catalog entry>}`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** when no definition of that name is visible from the workspace; **`400`** for a built-in or user-scope definition (nothing to approve), a malformed body, or a relative **`cwd`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/subagents/{name}/untrust`** | Withdraws the receipt of a definition for a workspace (same optional body). Withdrawing an approval that was never on file changes nothing. **`200`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** unknown name; **`400`** malformed body or relative **`cwd`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/hooks`** | Hook definition files a session with this workspace would load (**`?cwd=<absolute path>`**, default: the server's default cwd; a relative path is **`400`**), in load order (**`hooks.files`**: the operator's **`${FOXXYCODE_HOME}/hooks.json`**, then the workspace's **`.claude/settings.json`**, **`.claude/settings.local.json`** and **`.foxxycode/hooks.json`**). **`{"object":"foxxycode.hook_list","workspace","policy","items":[...]}`** where **`workspace`** is the canonical path receipts are keyed by, **`policy`** the effective **`hooks.project_trust`**, and each item carries **`file`** (the name receipts and the CLI use: the workspace-relative path for project scope, the absolute path otherwise), **`path`**, **`scope`** (**`user`**, **`project`**), **`digest`** (SHA-256 of the file), the trust decision for that workspace (**`trust`**, mirrored as **`trusted`** and **`needs_approval`**), **`error`** for a file that does not parse, **`warnings`**, and **`hooks`**: one row per handler (**`event`**, **`matcher`**, **`type`**, **`command`**, **`args`**, **`timeout_seconds`**, **`async`**, **`fail_closed`**, **`unsupported`**). Under **`deny`** project files are not read at all. See **`docs/features/hooks.md`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/hooks/trust`** | Approves the **current** content of a project-scope hooks file for a workspace: records a receipt in **`<home>/hooks-trust.json`** bound to the canonical workspace, the file and its digest, so its hooks run under **`hooks.project_trust: ask`** from the next turn. Rewriting the file withdraws the approval. Body **`{"cwd": ..., "file": ...}`**: **`cwd`** must be the session's **server-side** workspace (default: the server's default cwd), **`file`** the name **`GET /foxxycode/hooks`** lists. This route is the approval path for a remote console or ACP client, whose local `foxxycode hooks trust` writes a receipt on the wrong machine. **`200`** **`{"object":"foxxycode.hook_source","item":<catalog entry>}`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** when no such file is visible from the workspace; **`400`** for a user-scope file (nothing to approve), a file that does not parse, a missing **`file`**, a malformed body, or a relative **`cwd`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/hooks/untrust`** | Withdraws the receipt of a file for a workspace (same body). Withdrawing an approval that was never on file changes nothing. **`200`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** unknown file; **`400`** missing **`file`**, malformed body or relative **`cwd`**. |
| PUT | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}`** | Upserts one named entry in an mcp.json file. **`?scope=local`** (default) targets the project **`.foxxycode/mcp.json`** under the server's default cwd; **`?scope=global`** targets the user-global **`<home>/mcp.json`**. JSON body is the Cursor-format entry: **`command`**, **`args`**, **`env`** (object), **`url`**, **`headers`** (object), **`disabled`**, **`disabledTools`**. Requires **`command`** or **`url`**; **`400`** when the name contains **`__`**, spaces, or path separators, the scope is unknown, or the body is invalid. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**. Config.yaml-defined servers are edited via **`PUT /foxxycode/config`** instead. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/mcp/{name}`** | Removes the named entry from the mcp.json file that defines it (project or global). **`400`** for config.yaml-defined or unknown servers. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/workspace/files`** | Paginated workspace listing under session **cwd** (**`page`**, **`page_size`** required). Non-blank **case-insensitive** substring **`prefix`** on **`path_rel`**; omit or blank **`prefix`** yields empty **`items`**. **`dirs=true`** adds directory rows (**`kind`** **`dir`**, **`path_rel`** trailing **`/`**). JSON **`items[].name`**, **`items[].path_rel`**, **`items[].kind`** (**`file`** or **`dir`**), **`total`**, **`has_more`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/workspace/context`** | Workspace context for the composer chips: **`path`**, **`name`**, **`is_git_repo`**, **`is_worktree`**, plus **`repo_root`**, **`branch`**, **`branches`**, **`worktrees[]`** (**`path`**, **`branch`**, **`main`**) inside a git repository. Subversion is described independently in **`is_svn_repo`** and **`svn`** (**`available`**, **`wc_root`**, **`url`**, **`relative_url`**, **`repository_root`**, **`revision`**, **`branch`** as `trunk` / `branches/<name>`, **`branches`** when **`vcs.svn.branch_lookup`** is on, and **`nested`** when the working copy root sits above the folder), so a branch folder that also holds a git repository reports both. Uses the session **cwd** from **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`** (server default cwd without the header). Optional **`path`** query describes an explicit folder instead (pre-session preview); a missing folder yields **`400`**. Git and svn data degrade gracefully when the binary is absent or **`vcs.svn.enabled`** is off (**`is_git_repo:false`** / **`is_svn_repo:false`**). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/workspace/folders`** | Direct subfolders of **`path`** (default: session **cwd**) for the workspace folder picker: **`{"path","parent","folders":[{"name","path"}]}`**. Hidden folders and **`node_modules`** are skipped; rows sorted by name. Missing folder yields **`400`**. **`path=:drives:`** returns the machine's drive roots instead (**`{"drives":true,"folders":[{"name":"C:","path":"C:\\"}]}`**, **`path`** = **`parent`** = **`:drives:`**); on a host with no drive letters (Linux, macOS) the sentinel is just an unknown folder (**`400`**). A drive root reports **`"parent":":drives:"`**, which is how the picker walks up out of a volume — everywhere else **`parent`** stays the real parent directory. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/workspace/folders`** | Creates one subfolder for the folder picker: **`{"path","name"}`** makes **`name`** inside **`path`** (default: session **cwd**) and answers with the **listing of the new folder** (**`{"path","parent","folders":[]}`**), so the picker steps into it and **Open** picks it. **`name`** is a single entry: empty, **`.`**, **`..`**, a volume name, or anything containing **`/`** or **`\`** yields **`400`**. A parent that does not exist yields **`400`** and the chain is never created; **`path=:drives:`** yields **`400`** because the volume level has no directory behind it. A name already taken yields **`409`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/workspace/relativize`** | Body **`{"paths":[...],"uris":[...]}`** — converts absolute filesystem **`paths`** and/or **`file://`** / **`vscode-file://`** **`uris`** into workspace-relative POSIX paths under session **cwd**. Backs IDE drag-and-drop (dropped file → **`@`**-mention). JSON **`{"object":"foxxycode.workspace_relativize","items":[{"path_rel","ok"}]}`**; **`ok:false`** when the path is outside the workspace or the cwd root itself. Session picked via **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`** (default session cwd otherwise). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/onboarding/status`** | First-run onboarding probe for the embedded UI. Returns **`first_run`**, **`has_config`**, **`has_providers`**, **`has_models`**, **`has_agent_model`**, **`has_agent_credentials`**, **`missing_api_keys`**, and optional **`suggested_defaults`**. **`has_agent_credentials`** is true when the provider named by **`agent.model`** has a credential source: a non-empty **`api_key`**, an **`api_key_command`** (not executed by this probe), the conventional **`NAME_API_KEY`** variable, or a stored hub / ChatGPT login for the **`neuraldeep`** / **`codex`** types. **`missing_api_keys`** lists every provider with none of those; it is informational only. The SPA opens the provider picker once per page load when **`first_run`** is set, providers / models / **`agent.model`** are absent, or **`has_agent_credentials`** is false — a keyless provider the agent does not use does not reopen it. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/project`** | Current project folder. JSON **`{"object":"foxxycode.project","path","source","native_picker"}`**; **`source`** is **`project`** when a project was opened explicitly, **`default`** when falling back to the process cwd (**`-cwd`** / **`FOXXYCODE_CWD`** / startup dir). **`native_picker`** tells the SPA whether **`pick-folder`** can open the native OS dialog (desktop app). |
| PUT | **`/foxxycode/project`** | Body **`{"path"}`** — opens a project folder. The path must name an existing directory (**`400`** otherwise; **`503`** when the project store is unavailable). **New** sessions created afterwards use it as their working directory; existing sessions keep their own cwd. Also bumps the persisted recent list (`~/.foxxycode/projects.json`, capped at 15). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/projects/recent`** | Recently opened projects, most recent first. JSON **`{"object":"list","data":[{"path","name","last_opened_at","exists"}]}`**; entries whose folder vanished keep **`exists:false`** so the UI can dim them. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/project/last-session`** | Session to reopen for the current project. JSON **`{"object":"foxxycode.project_last_session","path","session_id"}`**. **`session_id`** is empty when nothing was recorded, or when the recorded session was deleted, is a scheduler run, or no longer lives under **`path`** (checked with the same **`cwd`** scoping as **`GET /foxxycode/sessions`**). Editor plugins get a fresh random port on every IDE launch, so this record — not browser storage — is what makes the panel reopen where the user left off. |
| PUT | **`/foxxycode/project/last-session`** | Body **`{"session_id"}`** — records the session against the current project in `~/.foxxycode/projects.json`. An empty **`session_id`** clears it, so the next launch starts on a new chat. Leaves the current project and the recent-list order untouched. **`400`** on a malformed id or body, **`503`** when the project store is unavailable. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/project/pick-folder`** | Desktop only: opens the native OS folder dialog owned by the app window and returns **`{"object":"foxxycode.project_pick","cancelled","path"}`**. Does **not** change the current project — confirm via **PUT** **`/foxxycode/project`**. **`501`** outside the desktop app, **`409`** while another dialog is already open. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/config/schema`** | JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the settings editor. Describes the same logical fields as **`ConfigJSON`** with **`description`**, **`default`**, **`pattern`** on **`providers[].name`**, optional **`x-foxxycode-*`** hints (for example **`x-foxxycode-provider-api-key-env-placeholder`** on **`providers[].api_key`** for dynamic placeholders), and **`x-foxxycode-property-order`** for section order. **`httpserver`** is omitted (listen bind stays on the **`foxxycode http`** CLI). **`GET`** / **`PUT`** **`/foxxycode/config`** still return the full document including **`httpserver`** when present in YAML. A section needing a Go build tag carries **`x-foxxycode-requires-build-tag`** (e.g. **`browser`**) in every build; the responding process adds **`x-foxxycode-build-tag-missing`**`: true` when its own binary lacks that tag, so the settings form renders the section read-only with an explanation instead of a dead switch. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/config`** | Current process configuration as JSON (same logical fields as **`config.yaml`**, including secrets). Per-session path fields (**`skills.dirs`**, **`subagents.dirs`**, **`hooks.files`**, **`prompts.dir`**, **`mcp_servers[].args`** / **`url`** / **`env`** / **`headers`**) are returned as written in the file, including a **`${CWD}`** placeholder; **`${FOXXYCODE_HOME}`** and the process-scoped directories are returned expanded. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/config/validate`** | Body is **`ConfigJSON`**. **`200`** with **`{"ok":true}`** when valid, **`400`** with **`{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`** otherwise. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/config/reasoning-levels`** | Reasoning levels the **`?model=`** logical id offers when **`models[].reasoning_levels`** is not overridden, for the settings form's **Fetch reasoning levels** button. Detection is model-id based (**`gpt-5*`** -> **`minimal,low,medium,high`**; OpenAI **`o`**-series, **`gpt-oss*`**, **`qwen3*`**, Claude extended-thinking -> **`low,medium,high`**). The provider type decides the Codex remap (**`minimal`** becomes **`none`**): optional **`?provider_type=`** carries the type of the provider row as it stands in the (unsaved) form and wins over the saved config, so a provider that is not saved yet, or whose type was just changed, resolves the way it will after Save; without it the provider prefix is looked up in the active config, and an unknown prefix gets the un-remapped list. The id need not exist in **`models[]`**, and a saved override is ignored - the button reports what the id offers, not what is configured. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"model":...,"levels":[...],"detected":true}`**; a model with no reasoning support is **`{"ok":true,"levels":[],"detected":false}`**, not an error; a malformed id is **`200`** with **`{"ok":false,"error":...}`** so the form can show it inline; a missing **`model`** parameter is **`400`** with the same flat **`{"ok":false,"error":...}`** body the other **`/foxxycode/config`** routes use. |
| PUT | **`/foxxycode/config`** | Body is **`ConfigJSON`**. Validates, writes **`config.yaml`** atomically, reloads in-process config for HTTP handlers and new agent turns. The file is rewritten **over its current content**: comments (including commented-out keys) and the existing key order survive the save, and a file that carries no **`# yaml-language-server: $schema=`** header gets the published one (**`https://hijera.github.io/foxxy-agent/config.schema.json`**) so editors keep validating it; a header pointing somewhere else is left as it is. Changed **`mcp_servers`** are reconnected for active sessions, re-running the workspace trust gate so an unapproved project declaration is not started; a session with a turn in flight is reconnected when that turn ends, not mid-turn; ACP client-provided per-session servers remain connected. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** on validation failure; **`500`** if the file was written but reload failed (server restores **`config.yaml.bak`** over the primary path when possible). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/models`** | Fetches the provider model list. OpenAI, Anthropic, and NeuralDeep use their model endpoints (NeuralDeep at the deployment its **`api_base`** selects); Codex uses the fixed official backend with the saved ChatGPT OAuth token. Credentials and **`proxy`** apply server-side. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"models":[{"id","name","vision"}]}`** on success; **`200`** **`{"ok":false,"error":"...","models":[]}`** when upstream fails; **`404`** for an unknown saved provider. **`vision`** is omitted unless the catalog advertises image input (**`capabilities.vision`**, or **`modalities.input`** containing **`image`**) and is advisory only - the SPA uses it to seed the **`models[].multimodal`** default. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/providers/models-probe`** | Model list for a provider **not saved in the config yet** (onboarding): body **`{"type","provider_name"?,"api_base","api_key","proxy"?}`** carries the credentials instead of resolving them by name (**`type`** is **`openai`**, **`anthropic`**, **`neuraldeep`**, or **`codex`**; empty **`api_base`** uses the type default, and **`api_base`** is ignored entirely for **`neuraldeep`** and **`codex`**). A Codex probe requires **`provider_name`** and reads the server-side OAuth credential for that name; no token enters the request body. Response shape matches **`GET /foxxycode/providers/{name}/models`** (including the advisory **`vision`** flag): **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"models":[...]}`** or **`200`** **`{"ok":false,"error":"...","models":[]}`** on upstream failure; **`400`** for a malformed body, invalid Codex provider name, or unsupported **`type`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/codex-auth`** | Non-secret OAuth status for a Codex provider: **`connected`**, optional **`source`** (`foxxycode` or `codex_cli`), and optional **`account_id`**. Accepts a valid unsaved provider name so Settings can sign in before saving the row. Never returns tokens. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/codex-auth/device`** | Starts ChatGPT device authorization and returns **`login_id`**, official **`verification_url`**, **`user_code`**, and **`status:"pending"`**. The saved provider's **`proxy`** applies. The exchange completes in the background and stores tokens under **`$FOXXYCODE_HOME/providers/<name>/codex-auth.json`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/codex-auth/device/{loginID}`** | Polls the server-side exchange. Returns **`status`** `pending`, `completed`, or `failed`, **`connected`**, and optional **`error`**. Never returns tokens. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/neuraldeep-auth`** | Non-secret NeuralDeep sign-in status: **`connected`**, display **`masked`** key, optional **`key_name`**, and **`source`** - the credential requests actually use (`oauth`, `api_key`, `api_key_command`, `env`, or `none`; an explicit key wins over a stored login). **`hub`** names the hub that issued the stored login and **`endpoint_hub`** the hub a sign-in for the endpoint in the optional **`?api_base=`** query (default: the saved row's, falling back to the default deployment) would use; Settings passes the endpoint picked in the form and warns when the two differ, since a key minted by one deployment is not honored by the other. Accepts a valid unsaved provider name, and a saved row of another type that the form has just retyped to neuraldeep (the credential file is keyed by name alone, so the widget works before Save; the row's own **`api_key`** / **`api_key_command`** still decide **`source`**). Never returns the key. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/neuraldeep-auth/device`** | Starts the hub's RFC 8628 device flow for client `foxxycode` and returns **`login_id`**, **`verification_url`** (the portal URL with the pre-filled code when the hub provides one, otherwise the plain verification URI), **`user_code`**, and **`status:"pending"`**. The hub is the one paired with the deployment: **`api_base`** in the optional JSON body (the endpoint picked in Settings, possibly unsaved), else the saved row's **`api_base`**; a body value that is not one of the two official endpoints is refused with **`400`** before the hub is contacted. A new start supersedes the provider's previous pending attempt, including one still waiting for the hub to answer (that one returns **`409`**); a sign-out cancels a pending start the same way. The saved provider's **`proxy`** applies. The server polls the hub in the background (bounded by the login's `expires_in`) and stores the key at **`$FOXXYCODE_HOME/providers/<name>/neuraldeep-auth.json`** with restrictive file permissions. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/neuraldeep-auth/device/{loginID}`** | Polls the server-side wait. Returns **`status`** `pending`, `completed`, or `failed`, **`connected`**, and optional **`error`**. Never returns the key. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/neuraldeep-auth`** | Signs out: best-effort revokes the key on the hub (**`POST /api/cli/revoke`**), then removes the local credential file. Returns the resulting status. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/providers/{name}/codex-auth`** | Removes only the FoxxyCode-managed token file. A separate Codex CLI login may remain as **`source:"codex_cli"`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/activity`** | Composer activity snapshot **`turnActive`** (exclusive turn lock), **`activitySeq`**, **`readActivitySeq`**, **`unreadComplete`**, **`permissionPending`**, and — for a session live in this process — **`messageSeq`**, the number of messages in its transcript. **`activitySeq`** advances once per *completed* turn; **`messageSeq`** moves **within** one, so a client polling a long turn can tell whether re-reading the transcript would return anything new. It is absent for a session only on disk: this route is polled, and it stays a disk probe rather than loading a bundle. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/tool-calls`** | Tool calls timeline; each **`resultPreview`** is capped at **19** content lines plus a final **`...`** row when truncated (20 visible preview rows total; see **`resultPreviewTruncated`**, **`resultTotalLines`**). Todo mutations (`foxxycode_todo_item_update`, `foxxycode_todo_plan_replace`) also include their final **`planSnapshot`** so historical cards retain the state they produced. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/tool-calls/{toolCallId}`** | Always full persisted **`result`** plus **`meta`** and **`args`**. The bundled SPA requests this when the user activates **More…** after the streamed or list preview was truncated (not when merely expanding the disclosure). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/background-tasks`** | Commands the agent started with **run_command** **`background: true`**. Each row carries **`id`**, **`label`**, **`command`**, **`status`** (**`queued`**, **`running`**, **`succeeded`**, **`failed`**, **`timed_out`**, **`stopped`**, **`orphaned`**), **`started_at`**, **`finished_at`**, **`exit_code`**, **`expected_seconds`** (the model's own estimate), **`timeout_seconds`** (the hard limit), **`notify_on_finish`** (the task wakes the agent when it ends), plus server-computed **`elapsed_seconds`**, **`overdue`**, **`running`**; the payload also has a **`running`** count. Tasks recorded by an earlier **`foxxycode`** process are merged in from the session bundle as **`orphaned`**. **Poll** this for status: a background task outlives the SSE stream of the turn that started it. See **`docs/features/background-tasks.md`**. Subagent runs started with **`spawn_agent`** appear as **`kind`** **`agent`**; such rows carry **`agent`** **`{name, session_id}`**, the definition name and the child session whose transcript **`GET /foxxycode/sessions/{session_id}/messages`** serves. An agent row also carries **`pending_permission`** while a **detached** child is blocked on a permission prompt: the payload of the SSE **`permission`** event (**`sessionId`** — the *child* session — **`toolCall`**, **`options`**) plus **`agent_name`** and **`asked_at`**. The parent turn that spawned the run has ended, so the prompt has no stream to appear in and is answered through **`POST /foxxycode/sessions/{child}/permission`**. Nothing is persisted: a prompt cannot outlive the process that raised it, so after a restart the run is simply gone. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/background-tasks`** | Clears the **finished** tasks of the session, in memory and from the session bundle, and answers with **`cleared`**. Running tasks are untouched. History is deleted with the session anyway; this is the operator's way to throw it away early. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/background-tasks/{task_id}`** | One task plus **`output`**, the combined stdout and stderr captured so far (works while it still runs). Optional **`?tail=N`** returns only the last N lines; a non-integer or negative value is a **`400`**. A task the pool no longer holds is answered from the session bundle log, capped at its last 256 KiB with **`output_truncated`** set. **`404`** when the id is unknown. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/background-tasks/{task_id}/stop`** | Terminates the task and the whole process group it started, then returns the final row and its output. Stopping an already finished task changes nothing and still returns **`200`**. An unknown id is a **`404`**; a task that exists but could not be terminated is a **`500`**, so "not found" never masks a process that is still alive. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/stats`** | Session stats: **`tokenUsageTotal`** (provider tokens **cumulative for the session**), **`tokenUsageByTurn`** (most recent turns; the overflow is folded into **`tokenUsageTrimmed`** so the total stays whole) plus the current **`contextBreakdown`**. Compaction rewrites the **`conversation`** / **`summary`** categories and the estimated total immediately while preserving provider counters, and the breakdown is persisted so a reloaded session reports the compacted window. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/debug`** | Debug-trace timeline (**`object`** `foxxycode.session_debug`, **`sessionId`**, **`events`**) collected only while **`debug.enabled`** is on (`--debug` flag or `debug:` config section): one record per **`turn_start`** / **`llm_request`** / **`llm_response`** / **`tool_start`** / **`tool_finish`** boundary with lightweight metadata (mode, model, message/tool counts, token usage, stop reason). Raw LLM HTTP request/response bodies go to the process log, not this endpoint. A session with no trace returns **`events: null`**. Guide: **[docs/operate/debugging.md](../operate/debugging.md)**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/assets/{name}`** | Raw bytes of a file from the session assets directory (browser-tool screenshots, pasted images). **`name`** must be a bare file name; path separators and traversal segments return **400**. The bundled SPA references this URL from browser-tool transcript cards. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/messages`** | OpenAI-shaped **`messages`**, optional **`memoryTurns`**, **`uiLog`**. After **`POST .../cancel`**, the last assistant row may appear on disk one persistence step later than the in-flight stream; clients that already showed partial text should merge with local state (bundled UI uses **`mergeTranscriptPreferLocalSuffix`** in **`external/ui/src/ui/chat/transcriptServerSnapshot.ts`**). For a child session spawned by **`spawn_agent`** the payload also carries **`readOnly: true`** and **`subagent`** **`{parentSessionId, name, taskId}`**: the transcript is served from the live child while it runs and from its bundle afterwards, and no route accepts a prompt for it (**`409`**), so the bundled UI replaces the composer with a notice linking to the parent chat. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/export`** | Renders the dialogue surface — **`user`** and **`assistant`** turns plus any assistant **`reasoning`** blocks; tool/system rows are omitted — into a downloadable attachment. Required query **`format`** is **`json`**, **`html`**, **`pdf`**, or **`docx`** (anything else is **`400`**). GitHub-flavoured markdown in message content is preserved across all three readable formats: headings, emphasis, strikethrough, links (PDF and DOCX keep the target as a real clickable annotation), nested lists, task lists, blockquotes, thematic breaks, syntax-highlighted code blocks, and **tables** — a pipe table becomes a drawn cell grid in **`pdf`**, a `<w:tbl>` with a repeating header row in **`docx`**, and a `<table>` in **`html`**. An image whose destination resolves to a file inside the session's own assets directory is embedded in the document (a `data:` URI in **`html`**, a media part in **`docx`**); a remote **`http(s)`** URL is **never fetched** at export time — that would let a download request drive arbitrary outbound traffic — and renders as a caption plus a link. The **`html`**, **`pdf`** and **`docx`** documents are meant to be read, so they drop the ambient editor state the agent appends to each user turn — the **`<foxxycode_ide_context>`** block (**Active File**, **Open Tabs**) and the **`<foxxycode_terminal_context>`** summary — keep the **`<foxxycode_terminal_output>`** wrapper the user asked for with **`@terminal`**, and render the **`<foxxycode_session_assets>`** uploads wrapper as an **Attachments** section (thumbnails for pictures, names for everything else) instead of printing its raw XML. A turn left empty by that removal is omitted. **`json`** keeps every wrapper verbatim: it is the machine-readable export, and a re-import wants what the model actually saw. The response carries **`Content-Type`** matching the format and **`Content-Disposition: attachment`** with **both** RFC 6266 parameters: an ASCII-only **`filename`** every client can read and an RFC 8187 **`filename*=UTF-8''…`** carrying the real title, so a Cyrillic name arrives intact instead of as literal `%D0%9E…`. The name is derived from the session title, falling back to the session id when the title has no usable ASCII form. **`404`** when the session holds no assistant answer yet — the same guard the bundled UI uses to hide the download action. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/export/file`** | Renders the same document as the route above but **writes it to disk** and answers **`{"path","delivered"}`** with its absolute path. Exists for the editor panels, which cannot save a download at all: IntelliJ's JCEF drops any download no **`CefDownloadHandler`** claims, and the VS Code panel hosts the SPA in a cross-origin iframe with no download permission. The file lands under **`<os-temp>/foxxycode/exports/{id}/`**, named from the session title, and re-exporting the same session and format **overwrites** it rather than piling up copies — unless that file cannot be written because something still holds it (Windows locks a **`.docx`** open in Word), in which case the next free **`<title>_1`**, **`<title>_2`**, … is used. **`409`** when every candidate name is held, so the caller can say the document is still open. The path is derived server-side and never accepted from the caller. Emits **`event: reveal_file`** on **`/foxxycode/ide/events`**; **`delivered`** reports whether any plugin was connected to receive it. Same **`format`** values and same **`400`** / **`404`** rules as the download route. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`** | **`text/event-stream`** relay of the live **agent**/**plan**/**docs**/**ask**/**debug** turn (same SSE as **`POST /v1/responses`** with **`stream: true`**). Replays bytes captured so far, then live tail until the turn ends. Like every SSE route here it answers with **`X-Accel-Buffering: no`**, so an nginx or corporate proxy in front of FoxxyCode does not buffer the turn into one late blob. Covers the **autonomous turn** a finished **`notify_on_finish`** background task wakes: it registers a relay of its own, so a chat open on that session watches it live instead of learning about it on the next reload. While the turn runs but no relay is registered yet, SSE comment **`: composer stream pending`** (about 30s max), then **`event: error`**. When no turn is in flight, answers **immediately** with **`event: error`** carrying **`error.code`** **`no_active_stream`** so the caller can fall back to the persisted transcript without waiting. Replayed frames carry an **`id:`** sequence; a reconnecting client sends it back as **`Last-Event-ID`** (or **`?last_event_id=`**) to resume after that frame. If those frames were already trimmed from the buffer, the stream leads with **`event: desync`** (**`{object, lastEventId, resumedAt}`**) so the client reloads **`GET .../messages`** rather than rendering a gap. The bytes of the primary **`POST /v1/responses`** stream are unchanged. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/assets/{name}/thumbnail`** | Bounded PNG preview of one uploaded image. The name comes from a user row's **`files[].preview_url`** in **`GET .../messages`**; original asset bytes are not served. Answers **`400`** for a name that is not a single path element. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/events`** | **`text/event-stream`** of activity that is not tied to one session: **`event: turn_started`** and **`event: turn_ended`** with **`{object, sessionId, phase, at}`**, for every turn in this server process whichever surface started it. On connect it replays one **`turn_started`** per turn already running, then **`event: ready`**; an idle stream sends SSE comment keepalives. Lets a client attach to a turn it did not start without polling **`GET /foxxycode/sessions`**. It also emits **`event: config_reloaded`** after every swap of the live configuration - a settings save, the agent's own **`config_commit`**, a skill install, an edit on disk that **`foxxycode serve`** picked up - so a client re-reads its config-derived lists (the model picker, the slash commands) without a page reload. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/permission`** | Resolves a tool permission prompt while a streamed ReAct turn is blocked. Body **`{"toolCallId","optionId"}`** where **`toolCallId`** matches **`event: permission`** on the composer SSE (**`toolCall.toolCallId`**). **`optionId`** is **`allow`**, **`allow_always`** (remembers this exact command), **`allow_always_program`** (offered for **run_command** only, and only when the command is a single plain invocation; remembers the program, or the program plus its subcommand for multiplexers like **git**), or **`reject`** (or send **`outcome`** **`allow`** / **`cancelled`**). **`204`** when accepted. **`404`** when nothing is waiting. Optional **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`** must match **`{id}`** when set. A child session spawned by **`spawn_agent`** normally holds no prompt of its own — its requests are relayed to the parent chat — and answers **`409`**. The exception is a **detached** child whose parent turn has ended: its prompt is published on the parent's background task row as **`pending_permission`** and is answered here under the **child's** id, the one its **`sessionId`** names. A **`409`** therefore only means nobody is waiting on that id. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/ide/events`** | **`text/event-stream`** side channel for native editor clients (e.g. the IntelliJ plugin) to render inline diffs. Process-global (one per workspace). Emits **`event: edit_proposed`** when a **`write`**/**`edit`**/**`apply_patch`** tool is awaiting permission (gated mode), and **`event: edit_applied`** after a successful write. Each **`data`** is **`{"type","toolCallId","sessionId","path","before","after"}`** with an absolute **`path`** and full file **`before`**/**`after`**. Resolve a gated edit via **`POST /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/permission`**. Also emits **`event: open_file`** (only **`path`** and **`sessionId`** are set) when the user picks **Show in IDE** on a plan card — see **`POST /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plans/{slug}/open-in-ide`**. Because it is user-initiated and the plan file lives in the session bundle outside the project, clients must open it without applying their in-project / native-diff filters. **`event: reveal_file`** carries the same fields and the same "outside the project, skip the filters" rule, but asks the client to select the path in the **OS file manager** rather than open it in an editor tab — it announces an exported transcript (**`POST /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/export/file`**), which is a PDF / DOCX / HTML / JSON download rather than source to edit. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/ide/editor-state`** | Native editor clients (VSCode extension, IntelliJ plugin) report the currently open tabs, the focused file, and optionally the current text selection. Body **`{"openFiles":["/abs/path",...],"activeFile":"/abs/path","selection":{"file","startLine","endLine","text"}}`** (absolute paths; **`openFiles`** may be empty, **`activeFile`** / **`selection`** optional; selection lines are 1-based inclusive, text capped server-side at 16 KiB). Process-global (one per workspace); the latest snapshot is injected into subsequent agent turns as a **`<foxxycode_ide_context>`** block (including a **`# Selection`** section, capped at 2 KiB) so the model knows which files the user is viewing. A non-empty selection also feeds the paste-to-chip copy ring (see **`/foxxycode/ide/paste-classify`**). **`204`** when stored, **`400`** on invalid JSON. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/ide/copy-buffer`** | IDE clients with real clipboard events (IntelliJ plugin) report each fragment copied in the IDE. Body **`{"kind":"file"|"terminal","path?","startLine?","endLine?","terminalName?","text"}`** — a file fragment carries the absolute source path and 1-based inclusive line range. Candidates land in a small process-global ring (5 entries, 15-minute TTL; blank or >64 KiB texts dropped) consumed by **`/foxxycode/ide/paste-classify`**. Like the rest of **`/foxxycode/ide/*`**, exempt from bearer auth (local IDE integration surface). **`204`** when stored, **`400`** on invalid JSON or kind. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/ide/paste-classify`** | The chat composer asks whether pasted text is a fragment recently copied in the IDE (paste-to-chip). Body **`{"text"}`**; optional **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`** selects the session cwd for relativization. Matching (after CRLF/LF normalization): exact match against the copy-buffer ring, then the current editor selection, then substring match against tracked terminal buffers. Response **`{"kind":"none"|"file"|"terminal","pathRel?","startLine?","endLine?","terminalName?"}`** — the composer inserts **`@pathRel:start-end`** or **`@terminal[:name]`** on a match. Single-line pastes under 16 chars, pastes over 64 KiB, and file paths outside the workspace answer **`kind:"none"`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/ide/terminal-state`** | Native editor clients report every open terminal. Body **`{"terminals":[{"id","name","shell?","cwd?","lastCommand?","output?","active?"}]}`** where **`output`** is a bounded tail of recent output. Process-global (one per workspace); the latest snapshot is injected into agent turns as a compact **`<foxxycode_terminal_context>`** block, and an **`@terminal`** / **`@terminal:<name>`** mention in the user's message expands to a fuller **`<foxxycode_terminal_output>`** block. Gated per IDE by the **`trackTerminals`** setting. **`204`** when stored, **`400`** on invalid JSON. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/ide/terminal-state`** | Returns the tracked terminals (**`{"terminals":[{"id","name","active"}]}`** — no output) so the SPA can populate the **`@terminal`** mention menu. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/completion`** | Inline code autocomplete for editor plugins: one LLM call with no tools, no session and no agent loop. Body **`{"prefix","suffix","path","language"}`** where **`prefix`**/**`suffix`** are the code on either side of the caret (**`path`** and **`language`** are prompt hints only). Both sides are truncated server-side to **`autocomplete.max_prefix_bytes`** / **`autocomplete.max_suffix_bytes`**, so a client may send more than it needs to. Per **`autocomplete.mode`** the hole reaches the model as native fill-in-the-middle tokens through a raw completion (**`POST /v1/completions`**; Qwen-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, CodeLlama, StarCoder and Codestral conventions are known) or as a chat prompt with two worked examples; in **`auto`** a raw call that fails switches that model to chat for the rest of the process. Up to **`autocomplete.related_files`** other open files inside the workspace (from **`POST /foxxycode/ide/editor-state`**) are excerpted into the prompt so the model sees neighbouring symbols. The server decides per request whether the caret invites a block (end of a line that opened one, or an empty line) or a single line, sends matching stop sequences (the exact next suffix line for a block, the line break for a line), streams the chat reply and cuts it where the block dedents past the caret's scope, then cleans it: fences, a re-typed caret line or indentation, and any tail already present in the suffix are removed; suggestions that are only closing punctuation or repeat the next line are dropped. Answers **`{"completion","model","mode","enabled"}`** with **`mode`** **`fim`** or **`chat`**; with **`"debug": true`** in the request the reply also carries **`raw`** (the model's text before cleaning), **`multi_line`** and **`stops`**. Models that reason before answering are handled too: stop sequences are matched by servers against the reasoning text as well, so the first empty answer that came with reasoning is retried once without stops and with the token budget raised to a 1024 floor (the reasoning alone outruns a normal suggestion budget), and the model keeps both afterwards (**`reasoning_retries`** in the stats) — though such models stay slow and budget-hungry here, and a **`-noreason`** variant is the better pick. The model is **`autocomplete.model`**, falling back to **`agent.model`** and then the first configured **`models[]`** row, with its **`max_tokens`** capped to **`autocomplete.max_tokens`**, sampling greedy unless **`autocomplete.temperature`** says otherwise, Qwen3 thinking pinned off, and retries disabled — a retried suggestion arrives after the user has typed past it. Cancel by dropping the connection: the upstream call is bound to the request context. A caret inside an identifier, or an empty buffer, answers an empty completion without calling the model. When **`autocomplete.enabled`** is false this answers **`200`** with an empty completion and **`enabled: false`** so clients stop asking, not an error. A model slower than **`autocomplete.timeout_ms`** yields **`200`** with an empty completion and **`"timed_out": true`**. A provider rate limit is passed on as **`429`** with **`Retry-After`** (seconds, from the provider's own hint when it gives one), so editors pause their automatic requests instead of paying for refusals — on the NeuralDeep hub each model is capped at 20 requests per minute, which continuous typing can reach; the prefix cache and the trigger filters are what keep a session under it. **`400`** on invalid JSON, **`502`**/**`503`** on LLM error/unavailability (including **`mode: fim`** with a model that has no FIM convention). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/completion/config`** | The subset of **`config.autocomplete`** an editor plugin needs before it starts asking: **`{"enabled","trigger","debounce_ms","multi_line","timeout_ms","max_prefix_bytes","max_suffix_bytes"}`**. Defaults are applied server-side, so a client never has to know them. **`trigger`** is **`auto`** (suggest while typing, after the debounce pause) or **`manual`** (only on the editor shortcut). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/completion/stats`** | Process-wide inline-completion counters: **`requests`** split by outcome (**`served`**, **`empty`**, **`errors`**, **`cancelled`**, **`timeouts`**, **`rate_limited`**) and by prompt mode (**`fim`**, **`chat`**, **`fim_fallback`** — raw calls that errored, **`fim_empty`** — raw calls that answered nothing; both re-issued as chat, and three empties in a row retire FIM for the model), **`reasoning_retries`** (chat calls re-issued without stop sequences for a model that reasons before answering), **`latency_avg_ms`** / **`latency_max_ms`**, **`prompt_tokens`** / **`output_tokens`**, and the editor-reported **`shown`** / **`accepted`** / **`dismissed`** / **`cache_hits`** with the resulting **`acceptance_rate`**. This is what decides whether the feature is worth keeping. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/completion/feedback`** | Body **`{"event"}`** with **`shown`**, **`accepted`** (Tab), **`dismissed`** (Escape) or **`cache_hit`** (re-rendered from the editor's prefix cache without a request). Fire-and-forget from the plugins; feeds the stats above. **`204`** when counted, **`400`** on an unknown event. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/question`** | Answers the interactive **`question`** tool while a streamed ReAct turn is blocked. Body **`{"requestId","answers"}`** where **`answers`** is an array of string arrays (one row per question, entries are option labels or custom text). **`requestId`** must match **`event: question`** on the composer SSE. **`204`** when accepted. **`404`** when nothing is waiting. Optional **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`** must match **`{id}`** when set. |
| PATCH | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}`** | **`{"title"}`** pins **`session.json.titlePinned`**. **`{"markActivityRead":true}`** advances **`readActivitySeq`** to the current **`activitySeq`** (clears unread dot in composer UI) **without** changing **`session.json.updatedAt`**, so the session does not jump in the history list. At least one field is required. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/workspace`** | Switches the session workspace. **`{"path":dir}`** moves the session **cwd** to an existing folder (skills, project rules, and slash commands are re-derived; new cwd persists in **`session.json`**). **`{"branch":b}`** checks the branch out in place; if the branch is already checked out in another worktree (including the main one) the session cwd jumps there instead. **`{"branch":b,"worktree":true}`** ensures a dedicated worktree (created under **`<home>/worktrees/<repo>/`**) and moves the session cwd into it. Session is created on demand (draft flow). The workspace is chosen **once per session**: as soon as the conversation has messages, any switch yields **`409`**. **`{"vcs":"svn","branch":b}`** switches the svn working copy in place (`svn switch`); Subversion has no worktrees, so **`{"vcs":"svn","branch":b,"worktree":true}`** checks the branch out into its own folder under **`<home>/worktrees/<wc>/`** (reusing an existing checkout) and moves the session cwd there. **`vcs`** defaults to **`git`**. Responds with the fresh workspace context (same shape as **`GET /foxxycode/workspace/context`** plus **`id`**). **`400`** for a missing folder, an unknown **`vcs`**, or a branch switch outside the corresponding repository; **`409`** on git checkout/worktree failures, svn switch/checkout failures, a disabled or missing svn client, or a locked workspace. **`409`** also for a subagent child session (`sub_…`), whose transcript is read-only and whose workspace belongs to its parent's turn. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/branches`** | Forks the session at one user message. Body **`{"userMessageIndex":N}`** (0-based over **`user`** rows). The new bundle receives every message **before** that user message, so resending an edited version of it produces a sibling conversation instead of overwriting the old one. Before forking, workspace turn diffs recorded **after** that point are **reversed** in the session cwd, so the files match the state the branch starts from. **`200`** **`{"object":"foxxycode.branch_created","newSessionId","branchIndex","totalBranches","fileRollbackNote"}`**; **`fileRollbackNote`** is human-readable (which turns were reversed, or why none were). **`400`** for a malformed id or a negative index, **`404`** for an unknown session, **`409`** for a subagent child session (`sub_…`), whose transcript is read-only and cannot be forked; branch its parent instead. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/branches`** | Branch points visible from this session, from **`branches.json`** in the session bundle. **`{"object":"foxxycode.branches","sessionId","branchPoints":[{userMessageIndex,currentIndex,total,sessions:[{sessionId,branchIndex,preview,lastUpdatedAt}],own}]}`**. **`own`** is **`true`** for a branch point this session introduced and **`false`** for the sibling view inherited from its parent. Sessions whose bundle no longer exists are skipped and **`currentIndex`** is derived from the surviving list, so a branch file written before deletion started pruning heals itself on read; a branch point with fewer than two surviving threads is not reported at all. The bundled UI renders each entry as a **`‹ n/m ›`** navigator under that user message. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/cancel`** | Best-effort cancel of an in-flight ReAct turn or streamed direct completion (**ACP `session/cancel`**). For persisted bundles, also writes a cross-process cancel marker so another **`foxxycode`** process holding the turn can stop cooperatively. When the LLM had already streamed assistant tokens, the agent **persists** that partial **`assistant`** row before ending the turn (**`StopReasonCancelled`**). Optional **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`** must match **`{id}`** when present. **`404`** when no live or persisted bundle exists under that **`id`** (session store required for cold loads). |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/compact`** | Summarize older session history on demand (coddy compaction engine). Optional JSON body **`{ "instructions": "…" }`** guides the summarizer. Forces compaction (folds whatever exists) and returns **`{ compacted, summary, compacted_messages, kept_messages, model }`**, or **`{ compacted: false, reason: "nothing_to_compact" }`** when there is no prior conversation. Equivalent to the built-in **`/compact`** prompt command. **`409`** when another agent turn holds the composer lock; **`400`** when compaction is disabled. A child session spawned by **`spawn_agent`** is a read-only transcript and answers **`409`** as well. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}`** | Removes the entire persisted session directory (including `tool_calls/` and `stats.json`) plus in-memory MCP clients. The delete covers the session tree: every child session spawned by **`spawn_agent`** is removed with its parent. |
| GET/PUT | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plan`** | Read or overwrite todo **`entries`** (ACP shape). |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plan/archive`** | Archives active todos like **`foxxycode_todo_plan_archive`**. |
| GET/POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plans`** | List or create design plan files **`plans/<slug>.plan.md`** (bundled UI; not core ACP). |
| GET/PUT/DELETE | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plans/{slug}`** | Read, autosave, or discard a design plan file. |
| PATCH | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plans/{slug}`** | Body **`{"runPlan":true}`** runs **`RunPlan`** (sync); **`409`** when the session is in **`ask`** mode. Prefer **`POST /v1/responses`** with **`metadata.runPlanSlug`** for streaming. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/plans/{slug}/open-in-ide`** | **Show in IDE** on the plan card: broadcasts **`event: open_file`** on **`/foxxycode/ide/events`** so the IntelliJ / VS Code plugin opens the plan file in its own editor. The absolute path is resolved server-side from the session bundle (callers cannot name a file); a plan missing on disk is **404** and nothing is broadcast. JSON **`{"object":"foxxycode.ide_open_file","path","delivered"}`** where **`delivered`** reports whether an editor client was subscribed. |

After **`PUT`** **`/foxxycode/config`**, the next **`agent`**, **`plan`**, **`docs`**, **`ask`**, or **`debug`** turn uses the updated **`models`**, **`tools`**, and other fields from the swapped in-memory config. **`mcp_servers`** changes are applied to idle active sessions before the save response completes and to future sessions; a session running a turn is reconnected when that turn ends. A reconnect that runs past the save's deadline leaves that session on the servers it already has and retries on its next turn, so one hanging server cannot strip the others.

### Session memory REST (**`-tags=http,memory`**)

These **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/memory/*`** routes register only when **`foxxycode`** is built with **`memory`** (**`external/httpserver/memory_http.go`**). A plain **`http`** build without **`memory`** returns **`404`** (**`memory_http_stub.go`**).

| Method | Path | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/memory/tree`** | Without **`root`**, lists **`global`** and **`workspace`**. Otherwise lists allowed **`.md` / `.txt`** children (traversal guarded). |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/memory/file`** | Query **`root`** + **`path`**. UTF-8 content. |
| PUT | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/memory/file`** | JSON **`{"root","path","content"}`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/memory/dir`** | JSON **`{"root","path"}`** for new subdirectory. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/sessions/{id}/memory/file`** | Query **`root`** + **`path`**. Removes a **`.md` / `.txt`** file or deletes a directory tree recursively. **`400`** when **`path`** targets the memory root itself. |

### Scheduler REST (**`-tags=http,scheduler`**)

Paths are **missing** from a plain **`http`** build and from OpenAPI when **scheduler** is not linked (client **404**). When linked, responses use the same **`ErrorEnvelope`** JSON as other **`/foxxycode`** routes. **`503`** when **`scheduler.enabled`** is false for that process. Handlers plus merged scheduler OpenAPI fragments live in **`external/httpserver/scheduler_http.go`** (**`http`**,**`scheduler`**); **`scheduler_http_stub.go`** registers nothing when **scheduler** is omitted.

| Method | Path | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| GET | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs`** | JSON **`{ scheduler, jobs[] }`**. Envelope **`scheduler`** includes **`enabled`**, resolved **`dir`**, **`timeout`**, **`max_queue`**, **`runs_active`**, **`retain_sessions`**. Optional query **`include_body=true`** embeds each job instruction body. Each **`jobs[].running`** is **true** only while this server process tracks an in-flight agent run for that job (not from a stray **`basename.lock`** alone). Stale locks older than a grace window are removed during list and daemon ticks. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs`** | Create job. JSON body **`job_id`**, **`description`**, **`schedule`** (5-field UTC cron), optional **`paused`**, **`cwd`**, **`model`**, **`mode`**, **`body`**. **`201`** + **`Location`**. **`409`** when **`job_id`** already exists. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}`** | Full **`SchedulerJob`** including **`body`**. |
| PUT | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}`** | Replace entire job file. |
| PATCH | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}`** | Merge fields (e.g. **`paused`**, **`schedule`**, **`body`**). Optional **`job_id`** in the body renames the on-disk job (moves **`.md`**, **`.state`**, **`.lock`** when idle). Response **`job_id`** is the effective id after the patch. **`409`** if the target id exists or the job is busy. |
| DELETE | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}`** | Remove **`.md`** and sidecars **`basename.state`**, **`basename.lock`** when idle. **`409`** when locked or a run is tracked. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/pause`** | Sets YAML **`paused: true`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/resume`** | Sets **`paused: false`**. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/run`** | Fire-and-forget manual run (**`202`**). Does **not** advance cron **`.state`** (cron timing stays independent). **`409`** when paused, busy, or locked. |
| POST | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/cancel`** | **`context.Cancel`** on the active tracked run when possible. If nothing is tracked but an old **`basename.lock`** remains (e.g. after a crash), the server may remove that lock and still set **`cancelled`** to **true**. JSON **`{ cancelled: bool }`**. |
| GET | **`/foxxycode/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/runs`** | Metadata for persisted runs (**`session_id`**, timestamps, **`status`**). **`limit`** query (default **50**, max **100**). Read full transcript with **`GET /foxxycode/sessions/{session_id}/messages`**. |

Process logs for scheduler should stay short; full traces live under **`sessions.dir`** in normal session layout with **`schedulerRun`** metadata.

## **`model`**, profiles, and direct completion

- **`POST /v1/chat/completions`** and **`POST /v1/responses`** require **`model`** to be exactly one **`id`** from **`GET /v1/models`** (session operating profiles **agent** / **plan** / **docs** / **ask** / **debug** or a **`models[].model`** entry).
- **agent** / **plan** / **docs** / **ask** / **debug** selects the FoxxyCode agent (ReAct, tools). Optional JSON **`metadata.model`** updates the session model selector, and **`metadata.reasoning`** updates its supported reasoning level. The agent maps the level to OpenAI **`reasoning_effort`**, Anthropic extended-thinking **`budget_tokens`**, or Codex **`reasoning.effort`** (`minimal` becomes `none`) with reasoning summaries and encrypted replay.
- **`model`** listing a **`models[].model`** YAML selector runs **one direct LLM request** per call (no ReAct); **`metadata`** with a **`model`** key on that branch is rejected with **400** (use **`model`** as the routing field only).

Non-stream replies include **`metadata`** with **`model`** set to the effective YAML backend selector (**`api_model`** may expose the REST model id).

## Sessions and headers

### Without **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`**

`POST /v1/chat/completions` / **`POST /v1/responses`** allocate a random session bundle for that flow (ACP **`session/new`**). The bundle's working directory is the **current project** (**`GET /foxxycode/project`**) when one is set, else the process default cwd. An explicit **`-cwd`** flag / **`FOXXYCODE_CWD`** at startup seeds the current project; otherwise the last opened project is restored from `~/.foxxycode/projects.json`.

### With **`X-FoxxyCode-Session-ID`**

1. Active in-memory bundle wins.
2. Otherwise load from disk when **`session.json`** exists.
3. Otherwise pin **`session/new`** with the supplied identifier (fresh empty bundle folders).

Malformed ids (**HTTP 400**). Dedicated **`/foxxycode/*`** helpers return **503** if persistence is unavailable (`Manager` lacked a **`FileStore`**, primarily in tests).

### Per-session mode and model (bundled UI)

- **`GET /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/messages`** returns **`mode`** (stored session profile: **`agent`**, **`plan`**, **`docs`**, **`ask`** or **`debug`**), **`model`** (effective YAML backend for the session), **`selectedModelId`** (stored override in **`session.json`**, may be empty), and **`selectedReasoning`** (effective reasoning level for the session, empty when the model has none).
- **`PATCH /foxxycode/sessions/{id}`** accepts **`mode`** to set the session profile (anything outside the five profiles **400**), **`selectedModelId`** to set the YAML **`models[].model`** selector for that session (unknown ids **400**) and **`selectedReasoning`** to set the reasoning level (must be one of the model's **`reasoning_levels`**; empty clears it; unsupported value **400**).
- The SPA restores **Model** from **`model`** and **Mode** from **`mode`** when opening a chat; a **New chat** starts in **`agent`**. Changing **Model** writes cookie **`foxxycode_llm_model`** (default for the next **New chat**) and **`PATCH`**es the active session; changing **Mode** **`PATCH`**es **`mode`** so the profile survives a reload even when no turn was sent. A turn writes the profile too, through the top-level **`model`** of **`POST /v1/responses`**.
- When the **server** changes the profile - **`metadata.runPlanSlug`** switching a plan run back to **`agent`**, or the model calling **`plan_exit`** - the turn's stream carries the named SSE event **`mode`** (**`{"sessionUpdate":"current_mode_update","currentModeId":"agent"}`**). It also replays through **`GET /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`**, so a client that reconnects mid-turn still sees it. A client that ignores this frame keeps posting the profile the session has already left, and the next turn writes that stale profile back.

## Authentication & CORS

Off by default (unchanged "no login" behavior). When **`httpserver.auth_token`** (or **`--auth-token`** / **`FOXXYCODE_HTTP_TOKEN`**) is set, every **`/v1/*`** and **`/foxxycode/*`** route requires **`Authorization: Bearer <token>`** and returns **`401`** with **`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`** otherwise. The SPA shell and static assets stay public; **`/docs`** and **`/openapi.*`** are protected unless **`httpserver.public_docs: true`**; the local IDE-integration routes (**`/foxxycode/ide/*`**) stay public so the editor plugin keeps working. The token is redacted from **`GET /foxxycode/config`** (reported only as **`auth_configured`**) and preserved on **`PUT`** when the payload omits it. Because EventSource cannot set an Authorization header cross-origin, the two SSE subscription routes - **`GET /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`** and **`GET /foxxycode/events`** - also accept **`?access_token=`**. A query string reaches access logs, proxy logs, browser history and `Referer` headers, so prefer a **stream ticket**: **`POST /foxxycode/stream-tickets`** (authenticated with the normal bearer header) returns **`{object, ticket, expiresIn, expiresAt}`**, and that ticket is accepted by the two SSE routes only, once, within 60 seconds. Set **`httpserver.stream_tickets_only: true`** to refuse the durable token in **`?access_token=`** entirely, so nothing that lands in a log stays valid.

Cross-origin access for a browser UI on another origin is controlled by **`httpserver.cors`** (**`enabled`** + **`allowed_origins`**, a single **`"*"`** allows any origin; bearer auth still applies). Preflight **`OPTIONS`** returns **`204`** before auth. The bundled UI can point at a remote **`foxxycode http`** via the environment selector (**`httpserver.remotes`**). See [remote-control.md](../plans/remote-control.md).

## Memory roots

Matches `external/memory/README.md`: **`global`** uses configured **`memory.dir`** (fallback **`$FOXXYCODE_HOME/memory`**). **`workspace`** resolves to **`$CWD/memory`** for that session bundle. **`agentMemory`** placeholders remain agent-only (`session.json`), not REST-editable here.

Interactive tool permission prompts are bypassed when **`tools.permission_mode`** is **`bypass`**. Otherwise the bundled UI shows **`event: permission`** during **`POST /v1/responses`** (**`stream: true`**) and completes the turn via **`POST /foxxycode/sessions/{id}/permission`** (same pattern as **`question`**).

## CLI flags

Equivalent to **`foxxycode acp`**: **`--config`**, **`--home`**, **`--cwd`**, **`--sessions-dir`**, **`--session-id`**, **`--log-*`**, optional **`--scheduler-enabled`**. Networking flags: **`-H` / `--host`**, **`-P` / `--port`**. Defaults fall back to YAML **`httpserver.host` / port** when left at **`0.0.0.0:12345`**.

## Build

```bash
# HTTP API only (no npm, no embedded SPA root)
make build TAGS=http

# HTTP API plus embedded SPA (**make ui-build** runs first)
make build TAGS="http ui"
```

`go test ./...` skips **`external/httpserver`** unless **`go test -tags=http`**. SPA-specific tests compile under **`go test -tags=http,ui`** (Makefile **`make test`** runs **`ui-build`** once, then a single pass with every optional module compiled in; **`make test-matrix`** and CI walk **`http`**, **`http,ui`** and the scheduler combinations one job at a time).

For a manual gateway check against a disposable **`foxxycode http`** process, **`examples/test_httpserver.sh`** runs the Python demos under **`examples/httpserver/`** (see **`examples/README.md`**). Steps that call chat or responses expect a working **`models`** backend.


# Reference / ACP protocol

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hijera/foxxy-agent/main/docs/reference/acp-protocol.md

# ACP Protocol Reference

## Overview

FoxxyCode implements ACP as the **wire contract for the harness**. ACP standardizes how clients (for example editors, scripts, or orchestrators) talk to an agent process. The stock configuration presents a **coding agent**, but transports and RPC methods are generic harness surface area - initialize, session lifecycle, `session/prompt`, permission flows, and MCP-related options.

Reference: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/overview

## Transport

All messages are newline-delimited JSON objects sent via **stdin/stdout**.

```
stdin  -> messages from Client to Agent
stdout -> messages from Agent to Client (responses + notifications)
stderr -> agent logs (not protocol messages)
```

## Message Types

### Request (Client to Agent)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "session/prompt",
  "params": { ... }
}
```

### Response (Agent to Client)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": { ... }
}
```

### Error Response

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": -32600,
    "message": "Invalid request"
  }
}
```

### Notification (Agent to Client, no response expected)

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "session/update",
  "params": { ... }
}
```

## Stdio clients (FoxxyCode-specific)

Hand-written scripts that drive **`foxxycode acp`** over a pipe should implement the following behaviors. Reference harness: **`examples/acp/acp_e2e_todo.py`**.

1. **Nil `result` and `omitempty`** - JSON-RPC success payloads are produced with `result` omitted when the Go handler returns a **`nil`** pointer (for example **`session/set_mode`**). A response line may contain only **`jsonrpc`**, **`id`**, and neither **`result`** nor **`error`**. Treat any object with a matching **`id`** and no **`method`** as the completion of your outstanding request.
2. **Interleaved `session/update`** - After **`session/prompt`**, the agent streams many notifications before the final response. Read stdout line by line until the line for your request **`id`** arrives; handle **`session/request_permission`** or **`session/request_question`** in between by writing a client response with the same **`id`**.
3. **Stdout buffering** - When stdout is not a TTY, output can be block-buffered. Wrap the binary with **`stdbuf -oL -eL`** (or equivalent) so lines appear as they are written.
4. **Concurrent request handlers** - Outstanding requests are dispatched asynchronously. Do not send a second RPC until you have consumed the response for the previous one if your client assumes strict ordering.

## Protocol Flow

```
Client                          Agent
  |                               |
  |-------- initialize ---------->|
  |<------- initialize resp ------|
  |                               |
  |-------- session/new --------->|
  |<------- session/new resp -----|
  |                               |
  |-------- session/prompt ------>|
  |<------- session/update -------|  (notifications: plan, available_commands_update, chunks, tool_calls)
  |<------- session/update -------|
  |<------- session/update -------|
  |<------- session/prompt resp --|  (stopReason: end_turn)
  |                               |
```

## Methods

### `initialize`

Negotiate protocol version and exchange capabilities.

**Request params:**
```json
{
  "protocolVersion": 1,
  "clientCapabilities": {
    "fs": {
      "readTextFile": true,
      "writeTextFile": true
    },
    "terminal": true
  },
  "clientInfo": {
    "name": "example-acp-client",
    "title": "Example ACP Client",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  }
}
```

**Response result:**
```json
{
  "protocolVersion": 1,
  "agentCapabilities": {
    "loadSession": true,
    "sessionCapabilities": {
      "list": {}
    },
    "promptCapabilities": {
      "image": false,
      "audio": false,
      "embeddedContext": true
    },
    "mcpCapabilities": {
      "http": true,
      "sse": false
    }
  },
  "agentInfo": {
    "name": "foxxycode-agent",
    "title": "FoxxyCode Agent",
    "version": "0.1.0"
  },
  "authMethods": []
}
```

### `session/new`

Create a new conversation session.

**Request params:**
```json
{
  "cwd": "/home/user/project",
  "mcpServers": [
    {
      "name": "my-mcp",
      "command": "/path/to/mcp-server",
      "args": ["--stdio"],
      "env": []
    }
  ]
}
```

**Response result:**

FoxxyCode returns both **Session Config Options** (preferred by modern ACP clients) and the legacy **`modes`** field for compatibility. Clients that support `configOptions` should use them for mode and model selection.

```json
{
  "sessionId": "sess_abc123def456",
  "configOptions": [
    {
      "id": "mode",
      "name": "Session mode",
      "description": "Agent executes tasks; Plan designs; Docs maintains markdown; Ask answers questions read-only; Debug diagnoses before fixing.",
      "category": "mode",
      "type": "select",
      "currentValue": "agent",
      "options": [
        {
          "value": "agent",
          "name": "Agent",
          "description": "Execute tasks with full tool access"
        },
        {
          "value": "plan",
          "name": "Plan",
          "description": "Plan and design without code execution"
        },
        {
          "value": "docs",
          "name": "Docs",
          "description": "Generate and update project documentation"
        },
        {
          "value": "ask",
          "name": "Ask",
          "description": "Answer questions with read-only research tools"
        },
        {
          "value": "debug",
          "name": "Debug",
          "description": "Diagnose issues systematically before fixing them"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "model",
      "name": "Model",
      "description": "LLM used for this session.",
      "category": "model",
      "type": "select",
      "currentValue": "openai/gpt-4o",
      "options": [
        {
          "value": "openai/gpt-4o",
          "name": "gpt-4o",
          "description": "openai"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "permission_mode",
      "name": "Permission mode",
      "description": "Controls when the agent asks for user approval before running tools.",
      "category": "permissions",
      "type": "select",
      "currentValue": "ask",
      "options": [
        {
          "value": "ask",
          "name": "Ask",
          "description": "Always ask before running commands or writing files"
        },
        {
          "value": "accept_edits",
          "name": "Accept edits",
          "description": "Auto-approve file writes; ask before running commands"
        },
        {
          "value": "bypass",
          "name": "Bypass",
          "description": "Never ask for permission"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "modes": {
    "currentModeId": "agent",
    "availableModes": [
      {
        "id": "agent",
        "name": "Agent",
        "description": "Execute tasks with full tool access"
      },
      {
        "id": "plan",
        "name": "Plan",
        "description": "Plan and design without code execution"
      },
      {
        "id": "docs",
        "name": "Docs",
        "description": "Generate and update project documentation"
      },
      {
        "id": "ask",
        "name": "Ask",
        "description": "Answer questions with read-only research tools"
      },
      {
        "id": "debug",
        "name": "Debug",
        "description": "Diagnose issues systematically before fixing them"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The `model` option is present only when the `models` list in the agent config is non-empty. The effective default model is `agent.model` until the user picks another model in the client, as described in [Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md). Each listed `value` matches the YAML `models[].model` string (`provider_name/api_model_id`).

### `session/load`

Reloads a persisted session by `sessionId`. The agent restores `session.json` and `messages.json`, rebuilds skills and MCP connections from the request, replays prior user and assistant turns (and tool call summaries) via `session/update`, sends a `plan` update if `todos/active.md` exists, and sends `available_commands_update` once the response is on the wire.

The replay precedes the response here, as ACP requires, and that is safe because the client named the session itself. Reopening a bundle through **`session/new`** (`foxxycode acp --session-id <id>`) is the other way round: the client only learns the id from the response, so the replay waits for it. Anything written earlier would arrive for a session the client has not registered.

**Request params** (per ACP, `cwd`, `sessionId`, and `mcpServers` are required):

```json
{
  "sessionId": "sess_abc123def456",
  "cwd": "/home/user/project",
  "mcpServers": []
}
```

**Response result:** `modes` and `configOptions` like `session/new`.

### `session/list`

Lists persisted sessions found under the configured sessions root (see README), newest first. The response includes `sessionId`, `cwd`, `title`, and `updatedAt` per entry; child sessions of subagent runs and scheduler runs are omitted.

The optional `cwd` narrows the list to one workspace. It names a folder, not a string: the path is cleaned, its symlinks are resolved when the folder exists, and Windows and macOS compare it case-insensitively. A session keeps the cwd its client gave it, and two clients often spell the same folder differently - the console stores the logical `$PWD` of a symlinked checkout while an editor sends the physical path it resolved, and a Windows client may lower-case the drive letter - so a session created by one is still listed for the other. Sessions of a parent or a child folder are not included: a console started in a subfolder of the workspace is not among the workspace's sessions. `foxxycode sessions list --cwd` and `GET /foxxycode/sessions?cwd=` apply the same rule.

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "session/list",
  "params": { "cwd": "/home/user/project" }
}
```

### Disk layout (FoxxyCode)

When the process is started with a writable sessions root (default **`$FOXXYCODE_HOME/sessions`**), each bundle is `<root>/<sessionId>/` with:
